message.content:
{
  "pattern_id": "P-LIT-GHA-CACHE",
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "rationale": "Add a cache step for Go module downloads using actions/cache@v4, keyed by runner OS and hash of go.mod and go.sum. This caches the dependency download state (~/go/pkg/mod) while preserving all existing install and test commands. The cache uses an exact key without restore fallbacks, and the original 'go mod download' step still runs on every execution (fast on cache hit).",
  "workflow_yaml": "'on':
  push: null
  pull_request: null
  workflow_dispatch: null
jobs:
  test:
    name: Test with Coverage
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@v2
        with:
          go-version: '1.26'
      - name: Check out code
        uses: actions/checkout@v2
      - name: Cache Go modules
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/go/pkg/mod
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-go-${{ hashFiles('go.mod', 'go.sum') }}
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          go mod download
      - name: Run Unit tests
        run: |
          go test -coverprofile=covprofile -coverpkg="github.com/88250/lute" ./...
"
}

I need to add a caching step for Go dependencies. The pattern says: "add a narrow trusted actions/cache@v4 step or configure caching on an existing setup action. Key it by runner OS and the best available checked-in dependency inputs (lockfiles when present; otherwise dependency manifests, Makefile/install declarations and workflow setup). Cache only dependency download state, use exact keys without broad restore fallbacks, and always run every original install and test command on cache hits. Do not skip work based on cache-hit outputs."

So I should add a cache step before "Install dependencies" that caches the Go module cache (typically `~/go/pkg/mod`). The key should include runner OS and hash of go.mod and go.sum (if present). I should include both if they exist. Since we don't have go.sum in context, but it's likely in the repo. I'll assume go.sum exists. The pattern says "lockfiles when present". For Go, go.mod and go.sum are the lockfiles.

I'll add a step using actions/cache@v4 with path: `~/go/pkg/mod` (or the Go module cache directory). The key: `${{ runner.os }}-go-${{ hashFiles('go.mod', 'go.sum') }}`. No restore-keys (exact key only). Then keep the original install step (go mod download) which will be fast if cache hit.
